clue.text: Background: what a lady may not wish to reveal about it

indicators.note: about means going around, so the first piece wraps the word it

parts.words: what a lady may not wish to reveal
parts.note: the old saw that a lady never tells her age: HER AGE
taken as written

explanation.surface: A discreet woman declines to discuss some aspect of her background.
explanation.walkthrough: The old saying holds that a lady never reveals her age; 'about' signals the wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: One's heritage is one's inherited background: family, tradition and origins.

clue.text: Some land already claimed, Russians excited, first of all

indicators.note: first of all means take the first letter of every one of the four preceding words

explanation.surface: Russians are thrilled to stake a claim to some territory already taken.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of land area, so a plot of that size is some land.

clue.text: Release of this undesirable unlikely, initially confined to accommodation in block?

indicators.note: confined to means held within, so the next pick is placed inside the accommodation

parts.note: a block of apartments contains flats

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of unlikely

explanation.surface: In a crowded apartment block, letting rip with wind would be most unwelcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes U from 'unlikely', and 'confined to' puts it inside FLATS. The definition leans on the whole clue: the thing whose release is undesirable.
explanation.definitionFit: Flatus is the medical word for intestinal gas, which polite company prefers kept in.

clue.text: Voice disagreement after brief collapse

indicators.note: after says the disagreement comes after the shortened collapse
brief means cut short, so the word for collapse loses its final letter

parts.note: to collapse is to fall
a set-to is a quarrel or fight

explanation.surface: A singer's voice gives out after a short collapse in some backstage row.
explanation.definitionFit: Falsetto is a high singing register above a man's natural range, a kind of voice.

clue.text: Cypriot man (Greek to me?), Giorgiou son of Georgios, for example

definitions.text: Giorgiou son of Georgios, for example

indicators.note: something that is Greek to me is unintelligible, a jumble, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A Cypriot explains a puzzling Greek naming custom in which a son's name follows his father's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek to me?' is the anagram signal, and it suits a clue about Greek names.
explanation.definitionFit: A patronymic is a name derived from one's father, as Giorgiou derives from Georgios.

clue.text: Flipping English cram onto perfect Greek island, visiting nightclubs etc

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: to cram is to fill
A1 means first-rate or perfect, with the 1 written as I
Cos (Kos) is an island in the Dodecanese

explanation.surface: A student crams English on a perfect Greek island while also out clubbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reverses E + FILL + AI + COS, so the island ends up at the front. A1 for 'perfect' gives AI, its 1 read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Going to clubs, bars and parties makes up one's leisure time spent with others.

clue.text: Acknowledgement came out: yours truly wrong?

indicators.note: wrong means incorrectly arranged, so the setter's name and the jumbled word are mixed together
out means not in its proper place, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: yours truly is the setter speaking of himself, and this setter is Paul

explanation.surface: An admission emerges: I, the writer, was mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yours truly' is the setter, Paul. 'out' already muddles CAME, and 'wrong?' mixes it with PAUL; the surface 'yours truly wrong' also echoes the confession itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means 'my fault', an admission of guilt or error.

clue.text: Having smuggled in drugs, a Mafia leader on Alcatraz moving cell

indicators.note: smuggling something in places it inside, so the gang takes the drug letter within it

parts.note: the Mafia is a mob
E is short for ecstasy, so drugs in crosswords

indicators.note: the leader on Alcatraz is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Mafia boss on Alcatraz smuggles drugs while being moved between cells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having smuggled in' puts E inside MOB. 'cell' looks like a prison cell; with 'moving' it is the definition, a living cell that crawls.
explanation.definitionFit: The amoeba is a single-celled organism that moves by extending pseudopods.

clue.text: Giantess, great runner

definitions.meaning: a tall, strong woman, after the legendary female warriors
a mighty river that runs through South America

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the mythic warrior women, hence a big strong woman, and South America's largest river.

clue.text: See 6
Flies in flight, perhaps, circling druggie in Australia

indicators.note: circling means going round, so the journey word encloses the rest

parts.note: a flight is one example of a trip, a journey

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the drug user sits within the short name for Australia

parts.note: Oz is a familiar name for Australia
a druggie is a drug user

explanation.surface: On a flight, insects buzz around an addict in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flies' looks like insects but means the opening on trousers. Oz is the informal name for Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Flies is the name for the fastening at the front of trousers, usually a zip or buttons.

clue.text: Savoury pudding crony fails to finish?

indicators.note: failing to finish means the word stops short, dropping its last letter

parts.note: read as crone-y, like a crone, i.e. like an old hag

explanation.surface: A friend leaves a savoury pudding half eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crony' is read as 'crone-y', like a crone, i.e. HAGGISH; the question mark flags that pun. 'fails to finish' drops its final H.
explanation.definitionFit: Haggis is Scotland's famous savoury pudding of offal, oatmeal and spices cooked in a sheep's stomach.

clue.text: Plastic bags Belgian hasn't opened, carrier of basket

indicators.note: plastic means pliable, easily reshaped, so the letters are remoulded
not opened means the first letter is missing

parts.note: a Walloon is a French-speaking Belgian

explanation.surface: A Belgian has left a pile of plastic shopping bags unopened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plastic' looks like a material describing the bags; it is the anagram signal, turning BAGS into GASB. 'hasn't opened' drops the W of WALLOON.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot-air or gas-filled balloon carries a passenger basket hanging beneath it.

clue.text: In acerbic manner, money invested in presidential coinage?

indicators.note: invested in means put inside, so the money goes within the coined word

parts.note: bigly is a word popularised by President Trump, so a coinage of a president
tin is slang for money

explanation.surface: Money is sarcastically ploughed into a president's commemorative coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coinage' suggests minted coins, matching 'money', but means a newly coined word, one Donald Trump made famous.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking cuttingly or sharply is being sharp-tongued, the sense of acerbic.

clue.text: Squat plastered in refuse — how stupid?

indicators.note: plastered in means stuck inside, so the squatting word goes within the refusal

parts.note: to refuse is to deny
to squat is to sit on one's heels

explanation.surface: A drunken squatter lies amid rubbish, wondering at his own idiocy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plastered' and 'refuse' suggest a drunk in garbage; 'refuse' is the verb, not rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Density can mean dimness or thickness of mind, so it measures how dim someone is.

clue.text: Percussion instrument, altering when beaten

indicators.note: beating something knocks it out of shape, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A percussion instrument changes its sound when struck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beaten' fits a drum, but here it scrambles ALTERING.
explanation.definitionFit: The triangle is a struck steel rod bent into three sides, played in the percussion section.

clue.text: Rodents cooler in student accommodation?

parts.note: a dorm, short for dormitory, houses students
ice cools drinks

explanation.surface: Mice are chilling out in a university hall of residence.
explanation.definitionFit: Dormice are small, bushy-tailed rodents known for long hibernation.

clue.text: Three quarters of team recognise shape

indicators.note: three quarters of a four-letter word keeps three of its letters, dropping the last

parts.note: a crew is a team, as of rowers
to scent something is to detect or recognise it

explanation.surface: Most of the squad can identify the form.
explanation.definitionFit: The crescent is the curved shape of a thin moon, a familiar geometric figure.

clue.text: In short film, female animal seen

indicators.note: In means placed within, so the female animal goes inside the short film

parts.note: vid is short for video
a ewe is a female sheep

explanation.surface: A sheep is spotted in a short movie clip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short film' is the abbreviation VID, not a short movie.
explanation.definitionFit: To have been viewed is to have been looked at, the past participle of see.

clue.text: Ground is wet in a country in Africa

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so the letters are pulverised and reformed

explanation.surface: The land is soaked in an African nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' reads as the earth; it is the anagram signal for IS WET IN A, whose letters all go into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Eswatini, formerly Swaziland, is a small kingdom in southern Africa.

clue.text: Saw not going to lose teeth, originally

indicators.note: to lose means to drop, so the letter is taken out

parts.note: staying means not going away

indicators.note: originally means take the first letter of teeth

explanation.surface: A saw that won't last loses its teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the cutting tool, with teeth; it is a proverb. 'originally' gives T, and 'to lose' drops it from STAYING.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or proverb, like 'look before you leap'.

clue.text: See 24
Therapist calling for sparkling water?

indicators.note: calling means saying aloud, so the answer sounds like the phrase

parts.note: fizzy eau, eau being French for water

explanation.surface: A therapist orders some bubbly mineral water.
explanation.walkthrough: Water here is the French eau, so 'fizzy eau' is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A physio is a physiotherapist, who treats injuries with exercise and massage.

clue.text: Times analogy failing to comprehend point, to say the least

parts.note: by is used for times in multiplication, as in two by three

indicators.note: to comprehend means to include, so the scrambled letters take the point inside
failing means breaking down, so the word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: W, west, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A newspaper's comparison falls apart because it misses the point, to put it mildly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' suggests the newspaper; it means BY. 'failing' rearranges ANALOGY, and 'to comprehend' puts W among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are emphatic qualifiers: by far, understating the case.

clue.text: Artful Dodger, say, best Dickens character

parts.note: the pick of something is the best of it
Herbert Pocket is Pip's friend in Great Expectations

explanation.surface: Dickens fans debate whether the Artful Dodger is his finest creation.
explanation.walkthrough: The Artful Dodger is the young thief in Oliver Twist, so the definition comes from Dickens too.
explanation.definitionFit: The Artful Dodger is a boy thief who steals from people's clothing on London streets.

clue.text: Channel going in deep I pulled towards the surface?

indicators.note: towards the surface in a down clue means read bottom to top, reversing the letters
going in means found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone digs deep and draws up something from far below.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going in' finds EPIP inside 'deep I pulled', and 'towards the surface' reads it upwards, as a down entry is read from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe is a tube that conveys liquid or gas, a kind of conduit.

clue.text: Release attention-seeker in relative, shortly

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the shout goes within the shortened relative
shortly means cut short, so the relative loses its last letter

parts.note: an uncle is a relative
oi is a shout to get someone's attention

explanation.surface: An attention-seeking family member is soon let loose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' drops the relative's final letter, leaving UNCL to hold the shout.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncoil a rope or spring is to unwind it, letting it loose.

clue.text: Ultimately, wad super fat

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter of wad

parts.note: ripping is old British slang for excellent or super

explanation.surface: In the end, a great wad of super fat.
explanation.walkthrough: RIPPING is dated British schoolboy slang for splendid.
explanation.definitionFit: Dripping is the fat that melts out of roasting meat, used for cooking.
